newsitem.title: USA: US West unit's $3.5 bln mega deal grabs spotlight.
newsitem.headline: US West unit's $3.5 bln mega deal grabs spotlight.

text.p: US West Inc unit US West Capital Funding's $3.5 billion multi-tranche debt offering grabbed the corporate bond spotlight once more as the deal was bumped in size for the second time in two days, to meet strong investor interest, dealers said.
"US West Capital's deal was launched at $3.5 billion; the deal had to be upped in size twice to meet demand for the paper," said one high-grade syndicate source.
-- $500 million in five-year notes with price talk seen at between 55 and 58 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $1.0 billion in 10-year debt with price talk seen between 80 to 83 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $1.0 billion in 30-year bonds with price talk at 107-110 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $500 million in 40-year bonds, puttable in the seventh year, with price talk between 56 and 58 basis points over Treasuries.
-- $500 million in 100-year bonds with price talk seen between 120 and 123 basis points.
Meanwhile, growing investor appetite for corporate debt paper and an improved financing environment continue to spur issuers into the primary market, dealers added.
"There's been a lot of demand for corporate paper driven by yields," said one syndicate source. "Recent issues have carried a decent spread."
Dealers noted that the majority of last week's issues tightened when freed to trade, an indication of how strong demand in the market for the paper has been.
"Most deals last week all tightened up on the break; investors continue to show strong interest in the corporate calendar," another syndicate source said.
This week's deals have also fared well, meeting with good investor demand, they added.

Among this week's issues, Philip Morris Cos Inc's A2/A rated 7.75 percent 30-year bonds, which priced to yield 101 basis points over Treasuries, are currently seen trading at 100 bid, 98 offer. The deal was upped in size to $750 million from an initial $500 million to meet strong investor demand.

Among upcoming debt offerings, Banque Nationale de Paris is expected to issue $350 million in 10-year notes via Salomon Brothers. The deal is expected to be launched on Wednesday, syndicate sources said.
Also, Leucadia National Corp is expected to tap the market with a $150 million 30-year capital securities deal which includes a 10-year call, dealers said.
TCI Communications Inc is preparing a $500 million trust preferred securities deal for one day this week via Lehman Brothers, sources said.
Growing demand for US West Capital's deal triggered the issuer to lift the size of the offering from its initially planned sale of $2.0 billion to $2.25 billion and add a fifth tranche, dealers said.
Still, investors craved more and the deal was bumped up to $3.5 billion.
The Baa1/BBB-plus deal is expected to price on Thursday via lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co.
The current breakdown on the five-part debt offering is as follows, syndicate sources said on Wednesday.
Baxter International Inc is expected to tap the market with a two-part $450 million A3/A rated debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The deal is expected to consist of a $250 million 10-year issue and $200 million in 30-year debt, sources said.
Quebecor Printing Inc is expected to tap the market with its first-time-ever debt offering, sources said.
The $150 million BBB-plus/Baa1 rated 10-year issue is expected to be underwritten by Goldman Sachs & Co and may price as early as Thursday, dealers said.
High-yield issuers are also expected to remain busy with offerings, dealers said.
CFP Holdings is expected to tap the 144A market with $110 million in seven-year guaranteed senior notes via NationsBank Capital Markets.
Imperial Credit Industries Inc is expected to issue $175 million in B1/B-plus rated 144A senior notes due 2007 via Lehman Brothers.
Vintage Petroleum Inc is expected to set $100 million in 12-year senior subordinated notes via Salomon Brothers.
Electronic Retailing Systems International Inc is expected to bring $100 million (proceeds) in 144A senior discount notes due 2004 via CS First Boston.
LDM Technologies Inc is expected to issue $100 million in 144A senior subordinated notes due 2007 via Smith Barney.
Tenet HealthCare is expected to bring a three-part debt offering consisting of $200 million in notes due 2003, $600 million in notes due 2005 and $500 million in notes due 2007, sources said.
The deal is expected to be underwritten by Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities.
